Your horse swings wide through the turn. You correct with your leg. He does it again.

Most North Texas barrel racers chalk that up to a training issue — or blame the footing.

Here's what Dr. Leo looks for first: rib cage mobility. When those joints lock up, your horse physically cannot bend through his body the way the turn demands. He compensates by drifting. Every time.

No amount of leg pressure fixes a structural restriction.

If your horse has been running wide and you've already ruled out the obvious, it's worth having Dr. Leo take a look before your next run.
